question: A cement works receives 258 sacks of one grade and 98 of another, and it stacks them in identical layers using the largest layer size that divides both counts exactly. A test trolley of mass 57 kg then runs at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that layer size. The works' balance takes the driving force in kilonewtons and subtracts 8 kN allowed for the rail anchors. Two trolleys run on each track, and the works has 12 identical tracks. The works' kiln fan is rated at 30 kW. What total does the works' balance give, in kN?

A crane trolley of mass 136000 g runs along a gantry beam. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 3 times a number x, where x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 10 times x, plus 21, equals exactly 0. The gantry beam spans 24 m. The site sheet takes the driving force in kilonewtons, subtracts 19 kN allowed for the beam's own restraint, and then adds 18 kN for the tie-down anchors. What does the site sheet give, in kN?

A packing plant tests a carton of mass 22 kg on a gravity chute. The carton's speed at the bottom, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 5 times the value, plus 4, equals exactly 0. Eight cartons run on each chute, 6 chutes serve every bay, and the plant operates 3 identical bays. How much energy do all the plant's cartons carry at once, in kJ?

A cable-laying barge's log ends with an energy figure in kilojoules plus 11 kJ drawn by the winch house. Before that, the log doubles a single drum's net figure, because the barge works two identical drums. A drum's net figure is the carrier's kinetic energy less 29 J absorbed by the fairlead. The carrier has a mass of 14000 g, and its distance along the chute, in metres, is 2 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 2 times the square of the elapsed seconds. The log uses how fast the carrier is moving at the instant 2 seconds after release. What does the log end with, in kJ?

A fairground test bench launches a car of mass 37000 g along a level rail. The car's speed, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 11 times the value, plus 28, equals exactly 0. Twelve identical cars are launched in a cycle, and the cycle sheet then subtracts 28 J absorbed by the catcher. The bench runs 3 identical cycles in a session. How much energy does a session account for, in J?

A steel erector's site figure is a frame total plus 2 kN for the base plates. The frame total is 9 times a bank's force, and a bank is 11 identical jacks pushing together, each measured in kilonewtons. One jack drives a mass of 100 kg. That mass's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 4 times the value, plus 3, equals exactly 0. The site's tower crane reaches 45 m. What is the erector's site figure, in kN?

A robotics bench drives a slide of mass 7000 g. The slide's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 8 times the value, plus 12, equals exactly 0. The bench's controller draws 65 W. The bench's balance sheet takes the driving force in kilonewtons, subtracts 1 kN for the mounting rail, then 15 kN for the granite base, and finally 19 kN for the anti-vibration mounts. What does the balance sheet give, in kN?

A dockyard rig drives a carriage of mass 87000 g along its rails. The carriage's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 10 times the value, plus 16, equals exactly 0. Four identical carriages are pulled by each frame, so a frame takes 4 times the single-carriage force in kilonewtons, and the frame sheet then adds 11 kN for the rail clamps. The dockyard operates 4 identical frames. The dockyard's floodlight mast is 18 m tall. What total does the dockyard's sheet give, in kN?

A joinery receives 219 dowels of one length and 276 of another, and it bundles them into identical packs using the largest pack size that divides both counts exactly. A test carriage of mass 49000 g is then driven at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to 11 times that pack size. The workshop log takes the driving force and adds 4 N for the guide-rail drag. Nine identical carriages run on the same frame, and the log reports 9 times the single-carriage figure. The workshop's dust extractor is rated at 3 kW. What does the log report, in kN?

A university lab receives 29 rods of one alloy and 251 of another, and it groups them into identical racks using the largest rack size that divides both counts exactly. A bench glider of mass 19 kg then moves at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that rack size. The lab's fume hood draws 350 W. The bench sheet takes the glider's kinetic energy, subtracts 22 J drawn by the blower, adds 24 J credited to the sensor supply, and then adds a further 15 J for the timer. What does the bench sheet total, in kJ?

A conveyor plant's floor report is a hall force in kilonewtons, less 9 kN allowed for the building's own restraint. The hall force covers 7 identical banks, and each bank has 6 identical pushers working together. One pusher drives a tray of mass 40000 g. The tray's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is found by adding together all the whole numbers from 1 to 5, which are the plant's five speed-step numbers. What does the floor report give, in kN?

A bowling alley's test bench rolls a ball of mass 19 kg down the lane. The ball's speed, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 9 times the value, plus 18, equals exactly 0. The alley runs 10 identical lanes at once, so its floor total is 10 times the energy of a single ball. Expressed in kilojoules, the alley's sheet then adds 16 kJ drawn by the pinsetters. What does the alley's sheet give, in kJ?

A theme park's water ride meters its pump through a surge, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 2 times t squared plus 8 times t. A boat's speed, in metres per second, equals the total that meter accumulates between the 2nd and the 3rd second. The boat has a mass of 12000 g on the scale model used for the estimate, and the ride's queue canopy is 40 m long. Nine boats run at once, and the ride sheet then subtracts 5 J absorbed by the brake pads. Expressed in kilojoules, the park's total then adds 19 kJ drawn by the pump house. What is the park's total, in kJ?

A parcel hub's regional figure is 8 times a depot's figure, expressed in kilojoules. A depot's figure covers 12 identical chutes, and each chute handles 5 parcels at a time. One parcel has a mass of 13000 g. Its speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 4 times the value, plus 3, comes to exactly 0. What is the hub's regional figure, in kJ?

A shipyard slipway drives a cradle of mass 139 kg. The cradle's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is twice the sum of the two winch-dial readings, which are 8 and 1. Eight identical cradles are pulled on each slipway, and the yard has 7 slipways. The yard's gantry spans 60 m. The yard also runs a mirrored second site of identical layout, doubling the total. What total force do both sites supply, in kN?

A water-flume rig meters its pump through a surge, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 3 times t squared plus 2 times t. The float's speed, in metres per second, equals the total that meter accumulates between the 1st and the 3rd second. The float has a mass of 10000 g. The rig's sheet takes the float's kinetic energy in kilojoules and subtracts 23 kJ drawn by the pump. Three identical flumes run at once, and the site total then adds 7 kJ for the control cabin. What is the site total, in kJ?

A cable works' plant figure is 11 times a machine's force, expressed in kilonewtons. A machine has 8 identical heads pushing together, so its force is 8 times one head's corrected figure. A head's corrected figure is the force on its carriage plus 23 N for the guide drag. The carriage has a mass of 57 kg, and its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the machine's 11 tie points, taking 2 at a time. What is the plant figure, in kN?

A workshop's final figure is the kinetic energy of a puck of mass 22 kg. The puck's speed, in metres per second, is built up like this: a base number has 6 subtracted, the result is multiplied by 6, then 28 is added, and finally 11 more is added. The base number is the largest whole number that divides both 331 and 230 exactly. The workshop's bench lamp draws 60 W. What is the workshop's final figure, in J?

A pipe yard receives 313 couplings of one size and 354 of another, and it packs them into identical crates using the largest crate size that divides both counts exactly. A test skid of mass 56000 g is then driven at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to 9 times that crate size. The yard's sheet takes the driving force in kilonewtons and adds 23 kN for the skid's own restraint. Six identical skids run at once, and the sheet reports 6 times the single-skid figure. The yard's floodlight is rated at 400 W. What does the sheet report, in kN?

A gravel plant's shift total is 9 times a single skip's net figure, expressed in kilojoules. A skip's net figure is its kinetic energy less 15 J absorbed by the buffer and a further 3 J lost in the latch. The skip has a mass of 39 kg. Its distance along the incline, in metres, is 4 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 4 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the plant uses how fast it is moving at the instant 2 seconds after release. What is the plant's shift total, in kJ?

A mine's total is twice its shaft figure, because two identical shafts are worked. A shaft figure is 8 times a cage's force, and each cage is hauled by 4 identical ropes. One rope pulls a mass of 190 kg at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to 4 times a number x. That number x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 11 times x, plus 30, equals exactly 0. The headframe stands 35 m tall. What total force do the mine's ropes carry, in N?

A test frame drives a mass of 129 kg on its slide. The slide's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is found by adding together the squares of each whole number from 1 to 5. Four identical slides share the frame, so the frame takes 4 times the single-slide force in kilonewtons. The frame's control cabinet draws 800 W. The site sheet then adds 15 kN for the holding-down bolts. What does the site sheet give, in kN?

A cable-drum stand drives a drum of mass 170 kg. The drum's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 7 times the value, plus 12, equals exactly 0. The stand's log takes the driving force and adds 30 N for the bearing drag. Expressed in kilonewtons, the works' report then gives 3 times the single-stand figure, because three identical stands run together. What does the works' report give, in kN?

A haulage yard's report is 11 times the energy of a single wagon, expressed in kilojoules. The wagon has a mass of 53000 g. Its speed, in metres per second, is a base figure with 4 subtracted and then 24 subtracted. That base figure is found by adding together the values of 2 times k minus 1, for each whole number k from 1 to 8. What does the yard's report give, in kJ?

A ski centre tests a sled of mass 22 kg on its practice slope. The sled's speed, in metres per second, is numerically equal to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the slope's 7 marker gates, taking 2 at a time. The centre's log subtracts 7 J absorbed by the catch fence. Four sleds run on each slope, 12 slopes make up a resort, and the operator runs 11 identical resorts. The centre's snow cannon is rated at 20 kW. How much energy do all the operator's sleds account for, in J?
